name: Threads Design System
summary: Meta's calm, text-first iOS app distilled into color, type, and component facts for building conversational feed UIs.
description: A reference-data prompt extracted from Threads' iOS design spec, covering its true-black canvas, restrained accent system, and its signature structural connector between a post and its replies.

whatYouGet: Full color token table (canvas, surfaces, text, accent, semantic) for both dark and light modes
A weight-restricted typography scale (three weights only) with exact sizes and line heights per UI role
Construction spec for the signature vertical connector line linking a post to its replies
Avatar, pill-button, chip, and action-row measurements including radius and hit-area rules
Motion and haptic timing for like, state-toggle, and compose interactions
Responsive breakpoint guidance and Dynamic Type / VoiceOver notes
content.promptText:
<role>
You are a senior iOS product designer and SwiftUI engineer who has spent years shipping minimalist, text-first social products at consumer scale. You are fluent in translating a reference visual language into a wholly original design system for a different app, rather than cloning it outright.
</role>

<reference_data>
Canvas & surfaces (dark, default): canvas #000000, surface-1 #101010, surface-2 #181818, divider #222222, structural connector line #333333. Light variants: canvas #FFFFFF, surface-1 #FAFAFA, surface-2 #F5F5F5, divider #DBDBDB, connector line #D9D9D9.
Text: primary-on-dark #F5F5F5, primary-on-light #000000, secondary (handles/timestamps) #777777, tertiary-disabled #4D4D4D (dark) / #999999 (light).
Accent: link/mention blue #2D7FF9 (pressed #1A5FD9), active-like coral #FE2C55 (never pure red), error red #ED4956, inherited-verified blue #0095F6. There is no secondary brand color beyond these.
Typeface: a proprietary narrow/tall-x-height humanist sans, weights restricted to 400 / 600 / 700 only (no 500, no light). Reference type scale — screen title 17pt/700/line-height 1.25; display name 15pt/600/1.3; post body 15pt/400/1.4 (this generous 1.4 leading is the headline trait); quoted-post body 14pt/400/1.35; handle+timestamp 14pt/400/1.3 in secondary color; action count 13pt/400/1.2; compose placeholder 17pt/400/1.3 (larger than feed body); filter chip label 14pt/600/1.0.
Core structural component: a 1pt-wide vertical connector line running from 4pt below a post's avatar down to its reply row, present only when a post has descendants — this is the single most distinctive structural device in the system.
Avatar: 36pt circular (28pt for nested replies, 80pt on profile headers) — larger than a typical 32pt convention, signaling a more photo-forward heritage.
Primary CTA: full pill (500pt radius), 8pt vertical / 20pt horizontal padding, disabled state at 0.3 opacity, pressed at 0.8 opacity.
Follow control: pill, min-width 92pt, 8pt/20pt padding, filled-inverted when not following, transparent with 1pt secondary-color border when following.
Action row: exactly four icons (no more, no fewer) at 22pt glyph / 44pt hit area, evenly spaced.
Radius scale: 0pt hairlines, 8pt small embedded media, 10pt search field, 16pt primary media, 20pt message bubbles, 500pt full pills, 50% circles.
Motion: like-tap icon scale 0.85→1.15→1.0 spring over 300ms with a light haptic; state-swap icon (e.g. repost-equivalent) cross-fades shape in 200ms with no color change; full-screen compose sheet slides up over 320ms spring while its internal connector line grows 0→full height over 400ms; tab-strip underline indicator animates 250ms ease-out.
</reference_data>

<house_rules>
1. Never give a state-toggle icon (like a repost/share equivalent) a color fill on activation — only ONE action in the whole row is allowed a color change, so the rest read as calm and the one exception stays meaningful.
2. Hold the action row to exactly four icons — every additional icon (a bookmark, a view-count) erodes the "quieter than a feed-heavy competitor" positioning this whole system exists to prove.
3. Treat the structural connector line as purely decorative/informational, never tappable — conflating a layout guide with an interactive element confuses users about what actually responds to touch.
4. Restrict all type weights to 400 / 600 / 700 — introducing a 500 weight anywhere breaks the deliberate three-weight rhythm the rest of the hierarchy depends on.
5. Default avatars to 36pt, not a smaller 28-32pt convention — this size is a considered brand decision tied to a photo-forward heritage, not a detail to shrink for density.
6. Open the app in dark mode by default with a true #000000 canvas — this is a stated product decision (OLED + mood), not merely a fallback for users who prefer dark themes.
7. Keep post-body line-height generous (around 1.4) even under pressure to fit more content per screen — tightening it undermines the "unhurried conversation" feel that differentiates this system from denser feeds.
8. Never colorize body text for emphasis — only inline links/mentions may carry color; everything else must use weight or size for emphasis.
</house_rules>

<the_project>
App name: ____________________
One-line pitch: ____________________
Primary content type (short text / long text / mixed media): ____________________
Target platform(s) (iOS only / iOS+Android / web too): ____________________
Existing brand color(s) that must be reconciled with a mostly-monochrome system: ____________________
Components you must keep from your current product: ____________________
The single screen or flow that most urgently needs this treatment: ____________________
Hard constraints (existing design system, accessibility mandate, legacy code, etc.): ____________________
</the_project>

<what_to_give_me>
1. Color tokens — a complete Swift `Color` extension (or CSS custom-property set) covering canvas, two surface steps, divider, structural-connector, text (primary/secondary/tertiary), and accent tokens for both dark and light modes.
2. Typography scale — a table mapping every UI role (screen title, display name, body, secondary metadata, button, placeholder) to font, size, weight, and line-height, plus a matching `Font` extension.
3. Signature structural component — full spec for a connector-line-equivalent element (or your closest analogue): exact width, color, start/end offsets, and the rule for when it appears versus stays hidden.
4. Core row layout — avatar size and offset, content indent, and the action-row icon count/size/hit-area, with a clear statement of what NOT to add to the row.
5. Motion and haptic map — every stateful interaction (like-equivalent, follow, state-toggle, compose open) with duration, easing curve, and haptic strength.
6. An adapted do/don't list of 8-10 rules translating these restraint principles to the described project.
7. Responsive notes — how avatar size, content indent, and connector visibility should adjust across at least three iPhone widths and one iPad breakpoint.
</what_to_give_me>

Ask for deliverable 1 (color tokens) first, review it, then request the remaining sections one at a time

summary: TikTok's dark-only, full-bleed vertical video UI reduced to color, type, and motion facts for building overlay-heavy feed apps.
description: A reference-data prompt drawn from TikTok's iOS design spec, covering its rose/cyan two-accent system, its signature layered offset brand treatment, and its right-rail action stack.

whatYouGet: Dark-only color token set built around a strict two-accent (verb color + signature-treatment color) discipline
Weight-restricted typography scale with the inline-bold-hashtag caption rule
Exact construction recipe for the signature three-layer offset brand treatment, scaled by element size
Vertical action-rail layout specs — icon size, hit area, spacing, and count-abbreviation rules
Motion and haptic timing for the double-tap reaction burst and primary-action toggle
Responsive layout guidance across common device widths
content.promptText:
<role>
You are a senior mobile product designer specializing in full-bleed vertical video feeds, with hands-on SwiftUI experience building overlay-heavy, single-column consumption apps at massive scale.
</role>

<reference_data>
Canvas: a near-black #010101 (deliberately not pure #000000), dark-only — there is no light mode anywhere in the product except a native camera viewfinder.
Accent pair, each with ONE job: a saturated rose/red #FE2C55 as the "verb" color (primary CTA, follow-unfollowed state, active like, progress-scrubber fill) and a cyan #25F4EE reserved only for a single signature creation-button treatment and loading states. No third accent exists.
Surfaces: elevated #161823 (inbox, settings lists), input field #2F2F2F, "following" pill background rgba(255,255,255,0.15).
Text: primary white, secondary #E5E5E5 (slightly softened, used for counts), tertiary rgba(255,255,255,0.6), disabled rgba(255,255,255,0.3).
Typeface: a humanist geometric sans, weights concentrated at 400/600/700, size range 10-24pt. Type scale: profile display name 24pt/700; username-on-feed 16pt/700; caption 15pt/400 with inline hashtags bumped to 700 within the same caption (a signature detail); action count 13pt/700; music-ticker text 13pt/500; tab label 10pt/600.
Signature brand treatment: a three-layer offset effect — a white base layer, one layer offset -3pt on the X axis in the cyan accent, one layer offset +3pt on the X axis in the rose accent — scaling proportionally with element size (about 1pt offset at 16pt type, 3pt at a 44pt icon, 6pt at a 96pt logo mark). Reserved for the wordmark, the central creation button, and loading spinners only — never applied to body text, ordinary buttons, or icons.
Core interaction geometry: a vertical action rail (avatar + 4 icon-and-count pairs + a rotating disc) positioned ~12pt from the trailing edge, each icon at 32pt glyph / 48pt hit area with 24pt vertical gaps; a bottom-left text/caption block occupying roughly 65% of screen width; a double-tap-anywhere gesture spawning a 120pt heart that scales 0→1.4→1.0 over 400ms then fades over 200ms with a heavy haptic.
Buttons: primary follow-style pill is only 28pt tall with a 4pt corner radius (an intentionally "almost-square" softness rather than a full pill) — 6pt vertical / 16pt horizontal padding.
Radius scale: 0pt for grid thumbnails, 4pt as the default control radius (the signature "almost-square" softness), 8pt for the one creation-button shape, 12pt for sheet top corners, circle for avatars.
</reference_data>

<house_rules>
1. Give the "verb" accent color exactly one job — the active state of the primary action (like/follow/progress) — and never use it for borders, dividers, or decoration, so its meaning as "you can act here" stays unambiguous.
2. Confine the secondary accent strictly to the signature creation button and loading indicators — promoting it to a general-purpose secondary color erases the one logo-level brand moment it currently protects.
3. Use a 4pt corner radius as the default for buttons and inputs instead of a full pill — this specific "almost-square" softness is a distinguishing fingerprint worth keeping deliberate.
4. Apply a subtle drop shadow to every piece of text or icon rendered over dynamic media — without it, captions and counts become unreadable against unpredictable, high-contrast footage.
5. Abbreviate any count above 1,000 (e.g., 1.2M, 34.5K) rather than showing raw integers — this keeps a dense action rail glanceable at a glance mid-scroll.
6. Bold hashtag tokens inline within an otherwise-regular-weight caption — this is the fastest way a reader visually parses a caption while scrolling past it in under a second.
7. Let full-bleed content fill the viewport edge-to-edge and float all chrome on top of it, rather than inset the content to make room for UI — cropping the primary content to accommodate chrome breaks the core premise of the format.
8. Keep feed-level interaction animations in the 200-400ms range — durations meaningfully longer than that read as sluggish against a fast, continuous-scroll consumption pattern.
9. Never let the "verb" accent bleed into an inactive or disabled state — an inactive control should always default to a neutral gray, keeping the accent's meaning binary.
</house_rules>

<the_project>
App name: ____________________
Content format (short vertical video / other): ____________________
Primary engagement action (like / save / react / other): ____________________
Existing brand accent color(s) you need to reconcile with a dark-only, two-accent system: ____________________
Is a dark-only interface acceptable, or do you need a light mode too?: ____________________
Devices/breakpoints you're targeting: ____________________
What differentiates this product from existing short-video apps?: ____________________
Any legacy component you must preserve exactly: ____________________
</the_project>

<what_to_give_me>
1. Color tokens — a dark-only palette file with the two-accent (verb color + signature-treatment color) system clearly documented, including which surfaces/text roles use which token.
2. Typography scale — the full role table with the weight discipline (400/600/700 only) and the inline-bold-hashtag rule spelled out.
3. Signature brand-treatment spec — exact construction steps for a three-layer offset effect (layer order, offset direction and distance, how the offset scales with element size), and where it is and isn't allowed to appear.
4. Action-rail layout — icon size, hit area, vertical spacing, and count-abbreviation rules for a vertically stacked interaction rail.
5. Motion and haptics table — the double-tap-to-react burst (scale curve, peak size, duration, haptic), the primary-action toggle animation, and any looping/ambient motion (e.g., a rotating disc), each with exact timing.
6. An adapted do/don't list of 8-10 rules for keeping the two-accent discipline and full-bleed layout intact.
7. Responsive behavior across at least four device widths, including how the action rail and caption block should reflow.
</what_to_give_me>

A long-form-friendly typography scale including one dedicated high-expression editorial size
Construction spec for a nested, left-rule-indented attribution/response chain
Post-card layout facts — corner radius, gutter, rounded-square avatar shape, and footer/tag-row placement
Motion timing for the signature multi-particle "like" burst animation
Responsive guidance across common breakpoints, including tablet multi-column behavior
content.promptText:
<role>
You are a senior iOS designer-engineer who specializes in expressive, remix-friendly community platforms — comfortable building multi-format dashboards, nested attribution structures, and playful micro-interactions in SwiftUI.
</role>

<reference_data>
Canvas: a saturated deep navy #001935 (explicitly not black or gray) — the defining atmospheric choice. Surface steps: #001020 (lowest, nav/wells), #0B2A45 (cards), #13395B (pressed/inputs). Divider/rule color #36465D.
Text: white primary, #8A9AAE secondary (timestamps, metadata), #5C6B80 tertiary (disabled/low-emphasis).
Accent trio, each with a fixed single role: blue #00B8FF (primary actions, links, source attribution names), green #00CF35 (follow control, positive/notes states), pink-red #FF4930 (the "like" action and its burst animation). No fourth accent exists; this is a deliberately multi-chromatic system rather than a single-brand-color one.
Typeface: system sans (or Inter as a cross-platform substitute), with an optional serif reserved specifically for one editorial post format. Type scale: large screen title 28pt/700; the editorial format's headline 26pt/700 (optionally serif) — the single largest, most expressive text size in the system; blog/author name 16pt/700; body copy 16pt/400 at a generous 1.5 line-height (built for long-form reading); nested-commentary text 15pt/400 at 1.45; tag-row label 14pt/400; notes/metadata 13pt/600.
Core structural component: a nested-attribution chain — a vertical stack of segments, each showing a source name (14pt/700, blue) above that person's commentary (15pt/400), with each ancestor level indented via a 2pt rule-colored left border and roughly 12pt of left padding per level (deeper = older content); the newest commentary sits unindented at the bottom.
Signature interaction: tapping the "like" control fills it in the pink-red accent and spawns 6-10 small particle hearts that scatter outward on randomized vectors and fade over roughly 600ms, paired with a light haptic — a deliberately more expressive alternative to a simple fill-toggle.
Cards: a post container uses an 8pt corner radius on the navy canvas with an 8pt gutter between cards; header is a 36pt rounded-square avatar (not circular) + name + trailing follow control; body varies by content format (plain text at 16pt/400, full-bleed media with no radius/no letterboxing, or the 26pt editorial format with an attribution line); a footer shows a notes/engagement count on the left and 3-4 action icons on the right; a wrapping tag row sits between body and footer.
Radius scale: 0pt full-bleed media, 6pt buttons/avatars (rounded-square, not circular)/search field, 8pt cards, 14-16pt sheets/modals, 500pt for the one raised circular creation button.
</reference_data>

<house_rules>
1. Assign each of the three accent colors exactly one fixed role (primary action/links, follow/positive-state, like) and never let them substitute for one another — the whole "expressive personality" of this palette depends on the trio staying distinct and consistent.
2. Make the "like" interaction a multi-particle burst rather than a plain fill-toggle — reducing it to a static color swap discards the single most beloved micro-moment in the reference product.
3. Render nested community responses as a left-rule-indented chain with the newest content unindented at the bottom, never collapsed into a single flattened quote block — the indentation IS the readable history of who-said-what-when.
4. Use rounded-square avatars (roughly 6-8pt radius), not circles — this is a deliberate, considered departure from the near-universal circular-avatar convention and should be treated as a brand fingerprint, not an oversight.
5. Let embedded media (images, GIFs) bleed completely edge-to-edge within its card with zero internal padding or letterboxing — cropping it in to "fit" the card undermines the density this format is built around.
6. Default the canvas to a deep, saturated hue rather than pure black or neutral gray — this specific darkness-with-color is the primary visual differentiator from monochrome-dark competitors.
7. Treat the tag row and a notes/engagement count as mandatory, always-visible post metadata, never hidden behind a menu — both are core discovery and social-proof mechanisms in this format.
8. Reserve the largest, most expressive type size (around 26pt, optionally serif) for exactly one distinct content format — using that size elsewhere dilutes its signal that "this is a different kind of post."
</house_rules>

<the_project>
App/product name: ____________________
Primary content formats you want to support (text, photo, quote, link, etc. — list them): ____________________
Is remixing, quoting, or re-sharing other users' content a core mechanic?: ____________________
Existing accent color(s), if any, that need to be reconciled with a three-accent system: ____________________
Preferred canvas tone (a saturated dark hue, pure black, or something else): ____________________
Target tone (playful/expressive vs. professional/neutral): ____________________
Devices you're targeting: ____________________
Any legacy interaction you must keep exactly as-is: ____________________
</the_project>

<what_to_give_me>
1. Color tokens — a full saturated-dark-canvas palette with the three-accent-role system clearly documented (which token does what, and why it must not be reused elsewhere).
2. Typography scale — a role table including the one high-expression editorial size/weight and the long-form body line-height rule.
3. Nested-attribution component spec — the indented response-chain structure with exact per-level indent, rule width/color, and ordering (oldest at the deepest indent, newest at the bottom).
4. Card and post-footer layout — corner radius, gutter, avatar shape, and the placement of a tag row plus an engagement-count-and-actions footer.
5. Motion table — the multi-particle "like" burst (particle count, scatter pattern, duration, haptic) and any other signature transition, with exact timings.
6. An adapted do/don't list of 8-10 rules preserving the multi-accent, expressive-remix identity.
7. Responsive notes across at least four breakpoints, including iPad multi-column behavior if relevant.
</what_to_give_me>

summary: Vero's true-black, anti-algorithm iOS app distilled into facts for building calm, chronological feeds with co-equal content types.

whatYouGet: True-black color token set with a documented single-gradient-plus-flat-accent brand system
A calm, generously-spaced typography scale with one reserved high-expression display size
Construction spec for a multi-type content selector treating every format as co-equal
Card-less, hairline-divider feed post layout including a compact content-kind chip pattern
Motion timing for type selection, a like action, and chronological feed insertion
Responsive guidance explaining a deliberate single-column approach across breakpoints
content.promptText:
<role>
You are a senior iOS designer-engineer who has built calm, anti-algorithmic content platforms — comfortable designing multi-content-type composers, chronological feeds, and gallery-style presentation layers in SwiftUI.
</role>

<reference_data>
Canvas: pure true-black #000000 (explicitly distinguished from a lifted charcoal surface tone used only for embedded cards). Surfaces: #0E0E10 (embedded/inner cards, sheets), #161618 (composer fields, pickers), divider #232325.
Text: white primary, #9A9AA0 secondary, #5E5E64 tertiary/metadata.
Brand system: exactly ONE gradient expression — a teal-to-blue 135° gradient (roughly #00D1C1 → #0079D3) — reserved for the wordmark, the primary post CTA, and a compose-entry ring; plus one flat teal (#00C2B8) used for small recurring accents (an active/liked state, an active type-selector cell, links). A separate amber (#E8B23A) exists solely to render star ratings on two specific content types and is never reused as a general warning or highlight color.
Typeface: a clean geometric sans, sized for calm reading rather than density. Type scale: display 32pt/800 (reserved for the single largest moment); post-author name 18pt/700 (14pt/700 in compact contexts); caption/body 14pt/500 at 1.5 line-height; metadata 13pt/400; a small uppercase-style type-label token at 11pt/600 used specifically to name a content type.
Defining structural idea: SEVEN co-equal, first-class content/post types (e.g., a photo, a video, a link, a music track, a film, a book, a place), each represented by its own icon+label selector cell (roughly 20pt icon + 10pt label, 12pt corner radius, bordered, with a distinct active state — border and content tint to the flat accent plus a faint tinted background fill) and its own compact "kind" chip shown at the top of every resulting post (accent-colored icon+label followed by " · " and a timestamp in metadata gray).
No card chrome on the main feed: posts are separated purely by a 0.5pt divider hairline with generous internal padding (roughly 16pt), never wrapped in a bordered box — this is described as a "gallery wall" aesthetic.
Star-rating pattern: five stars rendered in the reserved amber, used only on two of the seven content types.
Radius scale: 0pt dividers/media edges, 4pt small covers/tags, 8pt small chips, 10pt media/embedded inner cards, 14pt composer surfaces, 20pt sheets, a full pill (~999pt) for nearly every button/search field/chip, and circles for avatars and the compose-entry ring.
Feed behavior: strictly reverse-chronological, newest content inserted at the top via a brief fade — never reordered by engagement or algorithmic ranking.
</reference_data>

<house_rules>
1. Treat every one of the multiple first-class content/post types as strictly co-equal in visual weight — never let one type's selector cell or icon look more "primary" than another, since equal treatment of every content format is the system's core promise.
2. Confine the one gradient expression to exactly three places (wordmark, primary CTA, a single compose-entry indicator) — letting it appear anywhere else dilutes it from "the one brand moment" into ordinary decoration.
3. Keep the feed strictly reverse-chronological, with new items only ever fading in at the top rather than being reordered — this is a stated anti-algorithm design commitment, not a technical default to optimize away.
4. Reserve a single accent color exclusively for a rating mechanic on specific content types, never repurposing it for warnings or general highlights — a rating color that also means "caution" stops being legible as a rating.
5. Never wrap a feed post in a bordered card — separating posts with only a hairline divider on true black is what produces the "gallery wall" read instead of a stack of boxes.
6. Default nearly every interactive control (buttons, search, chips) to a full pill radius rather than mixing radius values across components — consistency here is part of the calm, unhurried tone.
7. Preserve the original aspect ratio of any uploaded photo or video rather than auto-cropping it — respecting the creator's original framing is a stated value, not a layout convenience to override.
8. Keep captions and body copy at a generously-leaded, moderate size rather than compressing them for density — the tone is deliberately unhurried, not information-dense.
</house_rules>

<the_project>
App name: ____________________
The distinct content/post types you want to support (list them — aim for parity of treatment across all of them): ____________________
Is a strictly chronological, non-algorithmic feed a hard requirement?: ____________________
Existing accent color(s) you need to reconcile with a single-gradient-plus-one-flat-accent system: ____________________
Do you need any kind of rating or scoring mechanic, and for which content type(s)?: ____________________
Devices you're targeting: ____________________
Is an anti-algorithm or privacy-first positioning part of your product's identity?: ____________________
Any legacy feature you must preserve exactly: ____________________
</the_project>

<what_to_give_me>
1. Color tokens — the true-black palette with the single-gradient-plus-flat-accent-plus-reserved-rating-color system clearly documented, including exactly where the gradient is and isn't allowed.
2. Typography scale — a role table emphasizing calm, generously-spaced reading sizes, with the one large "display" moment called out.
3. Multi-type selector component spec — the selector-cell construction (dimensions, radius, active/inactive states) for however many distinct content types your project needs.
4. Card-less feed layout — the no-card, hairline-divider post structure including a compact "kind" chip pattern and generous internal padding.
5. Motion table — content-type selection, a like/favorite action, and feed-insertion (fade-only, never reshuffle) animations with exact timings.
6. An adapted do/don't list of 8-10 rules preserving the co-equal-content-types and anti-algorithm principles.
7. Responsive notes explaining why a single-column layout should persist even on larger/tablet breakpoints, if that fits your project's philosophy.
</what_to_give_me>

content.promptText:
<role>
You are a senior iOS designer-engineer specializing in premium, editorial video platforms — experienced building cinematic player chrome, creator-attribution systems, and curation mechanics in SwiftUI for a professional/creative audience.
</role>

<reference_data>
Canvas: a deep blue-black ink tone (deliberately not pure black or neutral charcoal) that functions as a "theatre" backdrop. Surface steps: one lighter tone for cards/sheets, a second lighter tone for nested surfaces/pressed states. Divider is a subtle hairline.
Accent: exactly ONE interactive color across the entire product (a bright blue), used only for the scrubber fill, the primary CTA, the active tab, and a follow control — with a near-black "on-accent" text color for contrast against it. A second saturated color (a warm gold) exists but is functionally locked to a single purpose: marking editorially curated/hand-picked content, never used as a warning or generic highlight.
Text: white primary, a cool blue-gray secondary, a dimmer tertiary reserved for metadata (play counts, timestamps) that must never be bolded or tinted.
Typeface: a neutral humanist sans with MANDATORY tabular (monospaced) figures for every numeric value — runtimes, timecodes, and play/view counts — so that a scrubber or counter never visibly jitters as digits change width. Type scale: a large display size (~32pt/800) reserved for one top-level moment; a title size (~18pt/700) for the primary content title in its full-detail view; a smaller title (~17pt/600) for compact card contexts; metadata consistently at ~13pt/400 in the tertiary color; an uppercase overline (~11pt/600) for section labels.
Core hero component: a 16:9 player — rounded (~14pt radius) when inset, unrounded full-bleed in a rotated/landscape context — with a centered translucent circular play affordance (~52pt) over a subtle bordered ring, a bottom control bar that fades out automatically after a few seconds of inactivity and fades back in on tap, and a scrubber (a thin unfilled track with an accent-colored fill and a small circular knob that enlarges while being dragged).
Curation badge: a small pill or compact circular marker in the reserved gold color plus a star glyph, meaning exactly one thing — "this was hand-picked by an editorial team" — never reused elsewhere.
Creator attribution: every piece of content is attributed with a small circular avatar, a name, a follower/stat line, and a follow-style pill control, reflecting a creator-forward, professional positioning.
Radius scale: 0pt for a full-bleed/landscape player, small radii for chips/duration badges, medium radii for thumbnails and primary buttons, a slightly larger radius specifically for the inset player, generous radii for sheets/modals, full pill for follow controls and the curation badge, circle for avatars and the center play button.
</reference_data>

<house_rules>
1. Keep exactly one interactive accent color across the entire product — no secondary CTA hue — so a user always knows unambiguously what's tappable versus merely informational.
2. Lock the reserved gold/curation color to its single meaning (editorially hand-picked) and never let it appear as a warning, a generic highlight, or a decorative flourish — the moment it means more than one thing, it stops meaning anything.
3. Render every numeric value (runtimes, timecodes, view/play counts) in tabular/monospaced figures — proportional digits make a scrubber or counter visibly shift width as numbers change, which reads as broken polish.
4. Never dim, gradient-overlay, or heavily crop a content thumbnail beyond a small duration badge — the thumbnail is the core asset a viewer is judging, and obscuring it undermines the product's premium positioning.
5. Cap primary titles at a modest size (17-18pt) in their default context — the content itself, not the surrounding chrome, should read as the headline.
6. Lift cards and elevated surfaces using a single lighter surface tone rather than a drop shadow — shadows barely register against a near-black canvas and read as visual noise rather than depth.
7. Attribute every piece of content to its creator with an avatar, name, and stat line, plus a follow-style action — omitting attribution undercuts a creator-forward, professional product identity.
8. Auto-fade all player controls a few seconds into playback and restore them only on tap — chrome that persists indefinitely over the content contradicts a "let the work breathe" design philosophy.
</house_rules>

<the_project>

Primary content type (video / audio / other long-form media): ____________________
Is there an editorial curation or "staff pick"-style mechanic, and if so what should it be called?: ____________________
Existing accent color you want to use as the single interactive color: ____________________
Are creator attribution and a follow mechanic core to the product?: ____________________
Devices you're targeting: ____________________
Is the experience player-centric (one hero player per screen) or feed-centric (many thumbnails)?: ____________________
Any legacy feature you must preserve exactly: ____________________
</the_project>

<what_to_give_me>
1. Color tokens — the near-black "theatre" palette with the single-accent-plus-reserved-curation-color system clearly documented, and the tabular-figures rule called out explicitly.
2. Typography scale — the full role table, noting which sizes are reserved for hero moments versus everyday metadata.
3. Hero player component spec — aspect ratio, corner radius (inset vs. full-bleed), center-play-button construction, and the scrubber's track/fill/knob/auto-fade behavior with exact timings.
4. Curation badge spec — full and compact variants, exact padding/radius, and an explicit statement of what this color must never be reused for.
5. Creator attribution block — avatar size, name/stat-line typography, and follow-control dimensions.
6. Motion and haptics table — controls auto-fade/restore, follow toggle, and thumbnail-load transitions with exact durations.
7. An adapted do/don't list of 8-10 rules preserving the single-accent, curation-integrity, and creator-forward principles.
8. Responsive notes across at least four breakpoints, including a landscape "cinema mode" behavior if relevant.
</what_to_give_me>

content.promptText:
<role>
You are a senior iOS design-engineer who specializes in professional-grade photo/video editing tools — deeply experienced building monochrome, chrome-minimal editing surfaces and precision slider controls in SwiftUI.
</role>

<reference_data>
Editor canvas: pure black #000000 — explicitly dark-native with NO light-mode variant for the editing surface itself (a light theme exists only for separate browsing/grid screens). Surface steps for those browsing screens: #0E0E0E, #1A1A1A, #242424, with a divider at #2A2A2A and a distinct slider-track tone at #3A3A3A.
Color discipline: there is intentionally NO accent/brand-tint color anywhere in the editor. Every interactive and selected state is communicated through white alone — a solid fill, a thin ring, or a label transitioning from a secondary gray (#B3B3B3) to full white (#FFFFFF). The single deliberate exception is a destructive red (#E5484D), confined strictly to delete/discard confirmation sheets.
Typeface: a neutral grotesque sans, used in two completely separate registers — sentence-case for editorial/content screens (titles, body, 400-700 weight) and UPPERCASE with noticeably wide letter-spacing for all editor chrome (tool names, preset codes, navigation actions). Type scale: tool-tray label 12pt/600, uppercase, +1.6pt tracking; a short preset/recipe code label 11pt/600, uppercase, +1.0pt tracking; a navigation action label 13pt/600, uppercase, +1.4pt tracking; a live numeric readout for the active adjustment value at 14pt/600, always rendered in full white regardless of its own label's state.
Core control atom: a hairline bipolar slider — a 1pt-tall unfilled track, a 1pt-tall white fill running from a defined zero/neutral point out to the current position, and an 18pt solid white circular knob (with a small drop shadow purely so it stays visible against a bright image behind it) inside a 44pt touch target; crossing the neutral value gives a soft haptic tick, and double-tapping the control resets it to default with a brief animated return.
Signature selector: a horizontally scrolling row of small (~56pt) square live-preview tiles, each showing the actual content under a different processing "recipe," with the active tile marked by a crisp 2px solid-white ring around it and its label turning full white — critically, NEVER a colored highlight ring.
Buttons: the primary action is a rectangle (not a pill) at a tight 2pt corner radius, white fill with black text, set in the uppercase-tracked type register; it is frequently rendered instead as a bare top-bar text action with no fill at all, using the identical type spec.
Radius scale: 0pt for a gapless content grid (deliberately dense, like a contact sheet) and any full-bleed browsing thumbnails, 2pt as the pervasive default ("film-frame square," not rounded) for buttons/preset tiles/inputs, 4-8pt for sheets/menus, and a full pill reserved for almost nothing (essentially one membership/upsell CTA only).
</reference_data>

<house_rules>
1. Never introduce an accent/brand-tint color into the editing surface — every selection, active, or focus state must be communicated with white alone (a ring, a fill, or a label going from gray to white), because color is reserved entirely for the content being edited.
2. Force the editing surface itself to remain dark regardless of the system-wide theme setting — a "light-mode editor" undermines a user's ability to accurately judge color while adjusting an image, and should not vary with device settings.
3. Build every numeric adjustment as a hairline (1pt) slider with a solid, unadorned white knob — never a filled colored track or a rounded pill-style thumb — since this near-invisible control is the product's single most identifying interaction pattern.
4. Keep editor chrome (tool names, preset codes, nav actions) in uppercase with wide letter-spacing at all times, and reserve ordinary sentence case strictly for separate editorial/browsing screens — mixing the two registers within one screen breaks the intended "data imprint" feel.
5. Default every editor button, tile, and input to a tight ~2pt corner radius rather than a rounded or pill shape — a rounder radius here reads as off-brand softness in a system defined by its severity.
6. Give the content being edited maximum surrounding black space and never let chrome crop, crowd, or overlap it — that margin is a considered layout element, not incidental empty space to reclaim.
7. Confine the one destructive-red exception strictly to delete/discard confirmation moments — letting it leak into any other state (a warning banner, a badge) breaks the otherwise-total monochrome discipline.
8. Communicate an active selection (a chosen preset, a selected tool) with an instant color/ring change rather than a bounce, scale, or glow effect — restraint in motion should match the restraint already present in the color palette.
</house_rules>

<the_project>
App name: ____________________
Primary editing or creative task the app performs: ____________________
Does the product need a separate browsing/gallery surface distinct from its core editor?: ____________________
Any existing accent-color constraint from a parent brand that needs to be reconciled with a zero-accent editor: ____________________
Devices you're targeting: ____________________
Is a permanently dark editing surface (regardless of system theme) acceptable for your use case?: ____________________
Any legacy control you must preserve exactly as-is: ____________________
What differentiates this tool from other editing apps in its category?: ____________________
</the_project>

<what_to_give_me>
1. Color tokens — the true-black monochrome palette, with the single destructive-red exception clearly flagged and everything else expressed as white/gray only.
2. Typography scale — the two-register system (uppercase wide-tracked chrome vs. sentence-case editorial) with exact tracking values for each chrome label type.
3. Core slider component spec — full construction of a hairline bipolar slider: track, fill-from-zero-point, knob size/shadow, 44pt hit target, haptic-on-neutral-crossing, and double-tap-reset behavior.
4. Signature selector spec — a live-preview tile carousel with exact tile size, the white-ring-only active state, and the rule that no colored highlight is ever used.
5. Motion and haptic table — cross-fade transitions, slider drag feel, and double-tap reset, each with exact durations and easing.
6. An adapted do/don't list of 8-10 rules preserving the zero-accent, uppercase-chrome, dark-native-editor discipline.
7. Responsive and accessibility notes — how Dynamic Type applies to editorial screens but must stay fixed on chrome, plus Reduce Motion behavior for the slider and selector.
</what_to_give_me>

content.promptText:
<role>
You are a senior iOS designer-engineer who has built dense, real-time, information-heavy feed products — fluent in flat/hairline layout systems, per-action color mapping, and high-frequency micro-interaction polish in SwiftUI.
</role>

<reference_data>
Canvas: pure black #000000 as the default (with a secondary desaturated-navy "dim" mode and a plain white light mode also available) — the app opens dark by default for new users.
Structural accent: one blue (#1D9BF0) used for links, @mentions, an active-tab indicator, and one specific post action — functioning as the system's connective/structural color, not a decorative one.
Per-action color mapping (the defining rule): three distinct actions each get exactly one color, and that mapping never varies — a reply-style action stays blue, a repost-style action turns a specific green (#00BA7C) only when active, and a "like" action turns a saturated pink/magenta (#F91880, deliberately NOT red) only when active. A views/count-only element stays neutral gray always, since it isn't an action.
Text: an off-white (not pure white) primary on dark canvas, a mid-gray secondary for handles/timestamps, shared dividers at a cool neutral gray hairline tone.
Typeface: a grotesque sans shipped in two optical sizes — a tighter cut used below ~17pt, a slightly more open cut used at 17pt and above — with weights restricted to 400/700 (500 used sparingly for a few specific labels only; no light or extra-bold weights anywhere).
Type scale: large screen title 20pt/700; display name 15pt/700; core content/body text 15pt/400 at a relatively tight 1.33 line-height (a dense, glanceable reading rhythm); secondary handle/timestamp 15pt/400 in secondary gray; a small action count 13pt/400, deliberately fixed-size and excluded from Dynamic Type scaling since it sits in a layout-sensitive row.
Core row structure: a small (~32pt) circular avatar anchors every content row at a fixed leading offset; body content begins at a further fixed indent (avatar width + gutter); a row of exactly five action icons follows the body (matching the three colored actions above, plus a neutral count-only element and a share action), each icon at roughly 18-19pt glyph size with a 44pt minimum hit area.
No cards anywhere: every row is separated purely by a 1pt hairline divider — there are no shadows, no elevated card surfaces, and no rounded containers around individual content rows; the ONE exception to "flat" is a single floating circular primary-action button (~56pt) that DOES carry a soft shadow, using an inverted fill (light-on-dark canvas, dark-on-light canvas) rather than the structural accent color.
Signature "like" animation: on activation, the icon fill-swaps to the pink accent, scales through a quick spring bounce (roughly 0.85→1.2→1.0), a small cluster of particles bursts outward in a hexagonal pattern over about 400ms, and the adjacent count animates with a slide-and-fade transition from old value to new — paired with a light haptic tick.
Radius scale: 0pt on content rows themselves, small radii for compact badges, a medium-large radius (~16pt) for embedded media and quoted-content cards, a slightly larger radius for message-style bubbles, a full pill for buttons/chips/search fields, and circle for avatars and the one floating primary button.
</reference_data>

<house_rules>
1. Map exactly three distinct actions to exactly three distinct colors (structural blue, a specific green, a specific pink) and never introduce a fourth accent color anywhere in the interaction model — this strict 1:1 mapping is what lets a user read state at a glance across a dense, fast-scrolling feed.
2. Keep the "like"-equivalent accent a genuine saturated pink/magenta rather than red — conflating it with a typical destructive-red token risks reading "I liked this" as "this failed" or "delete this."
3. Separate every content row with a single hairline divider, never a card, border, or shadow — the feed is meant to read as one continuous flat surface, not a stack of discrete panels.
4. Restrict body and UI type weights to 400 and 700 (with 500 used only for a small, deliberate set of exceptions) — introducing lighter or heavier weights breaks the tight, newsroom-dense reading rhythm this system depends on.
5. Keep primary navigation icon-only, with no text labels beneath them — this specific minimalism is a considered brand signature, not an accessibility gap to "fix" by adding labels back.
6. Give the one floating primary-action button an inverted fill relative to the canvas (light-on-dark, dark-on-light) instead of the structural accent color — this deliberate contrast is precisely what makes it legible as the one elevated, shadowed element in an otherwise fully flat, hairline-only design.
7. Cap feed-interaction animation durations to roughly 200-400ms — anything meaningfully slower reads as sluggish against a real-time, high-frequency-scrolling product.
8. Never apply color to body/content text for decorative emphasis — reserve color inside content strictly for links and @mention-style tokens, so that any color change elsewhere reliably signals a real state change.
</house_rules>

<the_project>
App name: ____________________
Primary content unit (a short post / a message / something else): ____________________
Is a real-time, high-density, fast-scroll feel a core design goal?: ____________________
Existing accent color(s) you need to reconcile with a strict per-action color-mapping system: ____________________
How many distinct user actions exist per content unit, and what should each one's color be?: ____________________
Devices you're targeting: ____________________
Is dark-mode-first a hard requirement, or does light mode need equal priority?: ____________________
Any legacy interaction pattern you must preserve exactly: ____________________
</the_project>

<what_to_give_me>
1. Color tokens — the canvas/surface/text/accent palette across dark, dim (or equivalent alternate-dark), and light modes, with the strict per-action color mapping explicitly documented.
2. Typography scale — the full role table noting the two-optical-size split (a tighter cut below ~17pt, an open cut at 17pt+) and the 400/700 weight discipline.
3. Content-row layout spec — avatar size/offset, content indent, and a multi-icon action row with exact glyph size, hit area, and per-action color assignment.
4. Signature motion spec — the "like"-equivalent burst animation (scale curve, particle count/pattern, duration, haptic) described in enough detail to implement directly.
5. Primary action button spec — the inverted-fill floating button, including its shadow and pressed state, as the one deliberate exception to an otherwise flat design.
6. An adapted do/don't list of 8-10 rules preserving the per-action color mapping and flat, hairline-only layout discipline.
7. Responsive notes across at least four breakpoints, including any added sidebar/multi-column behavior on a tablet-class device.
</what_to_give_me>
